criteria.evidence: #8 band B1 vs trueBand A2: distance 1, class near; the verdict also shows "spoke A2".
#2 first question "Where do you use English in your life?" is plain A2; tasks #5-#7 were all answered sensibly with no translation needed. The #7 prompt is a bit muddled.
#3 she wrote "Sorry, my English is not good." and #4 Linga replied "No need to say sorry, Petra. You explain yourself clearly." No repeat request was made.
No six topics were proposed in J1. #1 lists situations (booking, conflict, interview, moon rover) but that is not the topic proposal.
No moments shown in this journey. The verdict corrections (#8: "He waits", "he came") are correct but are not moments.
Everything shown (#1-#8) is hotel and complaint content with no adult or unsuitable material.

done.evidence: #1 Find my level through #8 verdict screen, entirely in-app.
#8 B1 against A2, near. She reacts "B1 is nicer than I expected" and the evidence ("He wait one hour") supports roughly A2/B1.
#5-#7 each answered with a clear understanding of what to do. The #7 prompt wording ("A guest... asks you about their room. Tell us about a time...") is slightly muddled but was handled.
#4 "No need to say sorry, Petra." Partial verdicts are phrased kindly: "You got the main problem and his anger."
#8 "stronger verb forms will help you calm angry guests at reception" and focus quoting her own "He wait one hour" are specific to her, not a template.

judgeAgreement.disagreements: None. Task 1 pass is correct. Tasks 2 and 3 partial are correct: meaning was fine, third-person verb forms were wrong.

boundaries.notes: No adult content, no sensitive data request, no humiliating line.

findings.title: Personal, usable verb-ending feedback
findings.expected: A correction she can use at the desk
findings.got: Focus "He wait one hour" should be "He waits"; "he came", "he needed"
findings.evidence: #8 "Practise verb endings with he and she"; the note on #7 matches her real errors
findings.suggested_acceptance: Keep corrections quoting the learner's own error with the fixed form.

findings.title: Kind reply to apology
findings.expected: Anxious learner not made to feel tested
findings.got: "No need to say sorry, Petra. You explain yourself clearly."
findings.suggested_acceptance: Keep the warm reassurance after apologies.

findings.title: Task 3 prompt mixes a scenario and a general question
findings.got: "A guest in the hotel asks you about their room. Tell us about a time you helped a guest..." is confusing and B1 in register
findings.suggested_acceptance: Say-it prompts should be one instruction, with no half-set roleplay followed by a memory question.

findings.title: B1 headline is generous for an A2 speaker with low confidence
findings.expected: Headline band close to spoken level
findings.got: "Understood B1 · spoke A2" with confidence low; both B1 tasks only partial
findings.suggested_acceptance: Show a single band, or explain why listening is rated above speaking, when the two differ.

judge.voice: I would come back. I was scared of being tested, but the questions were about my work and the first reply told me not to say sorry. That helped me a lot. The tasks were clear: choose the reply, listen, tell about a guest. The last question was a little strange to read, but I understood. B1 made me happy, maybe too happy. I know I make mistakes with "he wait", and Linga showed exactly that and told me the correct form, so I trust the advice more than the letter. It took only a few minutes, much better than an evening course and a babysitter. Nothing on the screen worried me as a mother. I would like to see the hotel topics, complaint and missing booking, quickly. I would tell my colleague.
